greater_aegis_of_athena.name: Greater Aegis of Athena
greater_aegis_of_athena.unidentified_name: a bright tasseled shield with a snake-haired face at its center
greater_aegis_of_athena.lore: Homer's aegis is no ordinary shield. It is a goatskin hung with a hundred golden tassels, ringed with Rout and Strife and Terror, and Athena shakes it over armies to break their nerve. After Perseus cut off the Gorgon's head, he gave the head to the goddess, and she fixed it at the center. So the aegis carries the one face nobody could look at and live. Whoever bears it has little to fear from a stony stare, and those who strike at it may get one.

pridwen.name: Pridwen
pridwen.unidentified_name: a white round shield with a figure painted on the inside
pridwen.lore: Geoffrey of Monmouth arms Arthur for the battle of Badon with the lance Ron, the sword Caliburn, and a round shield called Pridwen. On its inner face was painted the Virgin Mary, so that the king had her before his eyes whenever he raised his guard. The older Welsh poets give the same name to Arthur's ship, the one he sailed into the Otherworld. Either way it carried him. The painted side is the side that faces the bearer, and spells break on the other.

tower_shield_of_ajax.name: Tower Shield of Ajax
tower_shield_of_ajax.unidentified_name: a massive laminated shield of ox-hide and bronze
tower_shield_of_ajax.lore: Homer says Ajax carried a shield like a wall, seven layers of bull's hide with an eighth of bronze hammered over them, the work of Tychius, the best leather cutter in Hyle. Hector's spear went through six hides and stopped in the seventh. When the Trojans reached the ships, Ajax stood on the decks alone and held them off with a pike. Achilles was the brilliant one. Ajax was the one who could not be moved, and neither can this.

scutum_of_aeneas.name: Scutum of Aeneas
scutum_of_aeneas.unidentified_name: a curved rectangular shield of divine workmanship
scutum_of_aeneas.lore: Venus asked her husband Vulcan to arm her son, and Virgil gives the shield he made most of a book. On it the god hammered things that had not happened yet: the she-wolf nursing the twins, the geese that saved the Capitol, the sea fight at Actium, Augustus in triumph. Aeneas admired the pictures without understanding one of them. Then he lifted onto his shoulder the fame and fortunes of his descendants. It turns a sword as well as it tells the future.

bronze_aegis.name: Bronze Aegis
bronze_aegis.unidentified_name: an ancient bronze shield, green with age
bronze_aegis.lore: The shield of a bronze giant, engraved with the eye of Hephaestus. The smith god made such guardians and set them to work. The most famous was Talos, who walked the shore of Crete three times a day and threw boulders at strange ships. One vein ran through him from neck to ankle, stopped with a single nail. The curved face of this shield sheds a crushing blow better than any iron of its age.

aegis_of_athena.name: Aegis of Athena
aegis_of_athena.lore: Athena's own shield, polished until it shows a face as clearly as still water. She lent it to Perseus for one purpose. He walked backward toward the sleeping Gorgon, watching her in the bronze, and never once looked at her directly while he swung. The shield has kept its shine. Down here a Gorgon who meets her own eyes in it fares no better than her victims did.

lionheart_shield.name: Lionheart Shield
lionheart_shield.unidentified_name: a battered steel shield engraved with a lion
lionheart_shield.lore: A steel shield engraved with a roaring lion and the motto DUTY UNTO DEATH. The name MARTEN OF THE IRON VALE is inscribed on the inside rim. It was carried into the dungeon four months ago by a knight who promised his wife he would be back for supper.

shield_of_the_spartans.name: Shield of the Spartans
shield_of_the_spartans.unidentified_name: a heavy round bronze shield painted with a red lambda
shield_of_the_spartans.lore: The round shield of the Spartan line, three feet of wood faced with bronze, marked with the lambda of Lacedaemon. Plutarch records what Spartan mothers said when they handed it over: come back with this, or on it. An exiled king explained the rule. A man wears helmet and breastplate for his own sake, but he carries the shield for the sake of the whole line, since its left half covers the soldier beside him. To drop it was the one thing not forgiven.

svalinn.name: Svalinn
svalinn.unidentified_name: a golden shield that radiates warmth
svalinn.lore: The Sayings of Grimnir name the horses Arvak and Alsvid, who drag the sun across the sky, and then the thing that stands between her and the world: Svalinn, the Cooling One. If it ever fell from its place, the poem says, the mountains and the sea would burn. A shield that shades the earth from the sun is not troubled by a dragon. Fire spends itself against it, and some of it goes back the way it came.

ancile.name: Ancile
ancile.unidentified_name: an oval bronze shield with an angular notch
ancile.lore: In the reign of Numa Pompilius, second king of Rome, a bronze shield fell out of the sky, and a voice said the city would rule as long as the shield was kept. Numa had the smith Mamurius Veturius make eleven copies so exact that no thief could pick out the true one. The twelve hung in the house of Mars, and the leaping priests carried them through the streets every March. This is one of the twelve. The arm behind it is strangely unhurried.

mycenaean_tower_of_telamon.name: Mycenaean Tower of Telamon
mycenaean_tower_of_telamon.lore: Before Ajax's famous tower, his father Telamon carried one like it on the first sack of Troy with Heracles. The Mycenaean fighter walked behind a shield as tall as himself, peering over the rim. Eight layers of ox-hide stitched to a wicker frame. Heavier than its bearer's torso. The body learned to lean into it the way a sailor leans into a mast.

pelte_of_the_thracian.name: Pelte of the Thracian
pelte_of_the_thracian.lore: The Thracian peltasts fought without armor, only this crescent shield of wicker and goat-hide. They skirmished, threw javelins, ran when the line came on. Greek hoplites scorned them as cowards until the Athenian Iphicrates trained peltasts who broke a Spartan regiment. The shield does not have to be heavy to win. It has to be light enough to leave with.

buckler_of_the_sumerian_lugal.name: Buckler of the Sumerian Lugal
buckler_of_the_sumerian_lugal.unidentified_name: a small round shield with cuneiform stamps
buckler_of_the_sumerian_lugal.lore: The Stele of the Vultures is the oldest picture of an army that survives. Around 2450 BC King Eannatum of Lagash beat the neighboring city of Umma in a quarrel over a field, and had the victory carved: his spearmen in a block, shields locked rim to rim, marching over the fallen while vultures carry off the heads. Lugal is the Sumerian word for king, and it means big man. The wedge marks stamped around this rim praise Ningirsu, the god of Lagash.

khopesh_breaker_of_thebes.name: Khopesh-Breaker of Thebes
khopesh_breaker_of_thebes.unidentified_name: a tall Egyptian shield of cowhide and cedar
khopesh_breaker_of_thebes.lore: Egyptian foot soldiers carried a shield shaped like a gravestone, flat at the bottom and rounded at the top, made of cowhide stretched over a wooden frame with the hair left on. A governor named Mesehti took forty wooden model spearmen to his tomb at Asyut, and every one holds such a shield with a different hide pattern. It was light, and tall enough to crouch behind. The sickle sword of the age, the khopesh, slid along its edge and found nothing to hook.

hittite_chariot_guard.name: Hittite Chariot-Guard
hittite_chariot_guard.unidentified_name: a waisted shield of dark hide, narrow in the middle
hittite_chariot_guard.lore: Egyptian chariots carried two men. Hittite chariots were heavier and carried three: a driver, a spearman, and a third whose only task was to hold a shield over the other two. At Kadesh in 1274 BC some twenty-five hundred of them forded the Orontes and broke into the marching column of Ramesses II. Both kings claimed the victory. Fifteen years later they signed the oldest peace treaty that survives. The shield is pinched at the waist so a spear arm can work past it.

assyrian_siege_pavise.name: Assyrian Siege-Pavise
assyrian_siege_pavise.unidentified_name: a tall wickerwork shield with iron strips
assyrian_siege_pavise.lore: In 701 BC Sennacherib of Assyria took the Judean city of Lachish and was proud enough of it to line a room of his palace at Nineveh with the carving. The reliefs show his archers working in pairs: one man draws, the other plants a wicker screen taller than both, curved back at the top to catch stones dropped from the wall. The carvings are in the British Museum. This is the screen. It is slow to shift and very hard to shoot around.

spartan_aspis_of_leonidas.name: Spartan Aspis of Leonidas
spartan_aspis_of_leonidas.unidentified_name: a heavy bronze hoplon with a lambda chased in gold
spartan_aspis_of_leonidas.lore: The king's own shield, its lambda chased in gold. Leonidas took three hundred Spartans to Thermopylae, every one a father of living sons. With them stood seven hundred men of Thespiae, who chose to stay to the end. Before the fight a local man warned that the Persian arrows would blot out the sun. Herodotus gives the answer to a Spartan named Dienekes: so much the better, we shall fight in the shade.

etruscan_round_shield.name: Etruscan Round Shield
etruscan_round_shield.unidentified_name: a bronze-faced round shield with a gorgon boss
etruscan_round_shield.lore: The Etruscans held Italy north of the Tiber when Rome was a cluster of huts. They gave the Romans kings, the arch, the triumph, and the rods and axe carried before a magistrate. Scholars can sound out their writing but can translate only a little of it. Their painted tombs show heavy infantry behind round shields faced with bronze, fighting in the Greek manner. Rome learned the phalanx from them and then swallowed them whole. The Gorgon on the boss came from Greece too.

scutum_of_the_legio.name: Scutum of the Legio
scutum_of_the_legio.unidentified_name: a curved red rectangular shield with gold wings
scutum_of_the_legio.lore: The Twelfth Legion, called Fulminata, carried the thunderbolt as its badge. Its shield was plywood: three layers of thin strips glued with the grain crossed, covered in hide and linen, bound at the rim, with an iron boss over the grip. It was curved to wrap the body. Locked overhead and on every side it made the tortoise, a formation that walked up to city walls under a rain of missiles. A tradesman built this one, and an empire was won behind his work.

macedonian_aspis_of_philip.name: Macedonian Aspis of Philip
macedonian_aspis_of_philip.unidentified_name: a small concave shield with a sunburst
macedonian_aspis_of_philip.lore: Philip II gave his infantry the sarissa, a pike eighteen feet long that needed both hands. So the shield had to shrink. He hung a small bronze bowl from a neck strap and slipped it over the left forearm, leaving the hand free for the shaft. Five rows of pike points reached past the front rank. His son Alexander took that hedge of spears to the Indus. The burst of rays on the face is the star of the Macedonian kings, and it throws back a little fire.

celtic_oval_shield.name: Celtic Oval Shield
celtic_oval_shield.unidentified_name: an oval wooden shield with a spiral boss
celtic_oval_shield.lore: The Gauls carried long oval shields of wood, painted with whorls, with an iron boss over the grip. Caesar describes what happened when the Helvetii locked them together and advanced: the Roman javelins punched through two shields at a time and pinned them to each other, the soft iron shanks bent, and the warriors could neither pull them out nor fight with a left arm so burdened. Many threw their shields away. Against a sword edge, the oak does much better.

germanic_kriegsschild.name: Germanic Kriegsschild
germanic_kriegsschild.unidentified_name: a planked round shield with a fur-wrapped rim
germanic_kriegsschild.lore: Tacitus wrote that the German tribes carried little iron, and painted their shields in chosen colors. A warrior who left his shield on the field was barred from sacrifice and council, the deepest disgrace they knew. In AD 9 Arminius led three Roman legions into the Teutoburg Forest and destroyed them over three days. Augustus is said to have beaten his head on a door and shouted for his legions back. The planks are northern pine and do not mind the cold.

sarmatian_lamellar_targe.name: Sarmatian Lamellar Targe
sarmatian_lamellar_targe.unidentified_name: a small lacquered shield of overlapping scales
sarmatian_lamellar_targe.lore: The Sarmatians were horse nomads of the steppe who armored rider and mount alike in overlapping scales, sometimes cut from horn or hoof when iron was scarce. Marcus Aurelius beat them on the frozen Danube and took eight thousand of their cavalry into Roman service. He sent fifty-five hundred of them to Britain. Some scholars think their dragon banners and their stories of a sword in the ground lingered there long enough to color the legend of Arthur.

battersea_votive_shield.name: Battersea Votive Shield
battersea_votive_shield.unidentified_name: a thin bronze shield set with red glass studs
battersea_votive_shield.lore: Workmen dredged it from the Thames at Battersea in 1857: a facing of sheet bronze worked in flowing curves and set with twenty-seven studs of red glass. It is too thin and too short to have stopped a spear. The Britons of the Iron Age made it to give away. They took the finest thing their smiths could make and dropped it in the river for a god whose name nobody wrote down. A gift like that still has a claim on unseen things.

saxon_round_shield.name: Saxon Round Shield
saxon_round_shield.unidentified_name: a round limewood shield with gilded beast fittings
saxon_round_shield.lore: The great ship burial at Sutton Hoo held a shield of limewood boards covered in hide, with a heavy iron boss and gilded fittings in the shapes of a dragon and a bird of prey. Most scholars think the man buried there was Raedwald, king of the East Angles, who died about 624. The poets of his people called a shield simply 'the linden,' and their battle line was the shield wall, rim over rim. This is the kind of board the Beowulf poet was thinking of.

lendings_of_beowulf.name: Lendings of Beowulf
lendings_of_beowulf.unidentified_name: a round shield of solid iron, scorched blue at the rim
lendings_of_beowulf.lore: Beowulf had ruled the Geats fifty years when a thief stole a cup from a dragon's hoard and the dragon burned his hall. The old king knew a linden shield would not last against that breath, so he ordered one made entirely of iron. He took eleven companions and the thief to show the way. When the fire came, ten ran for the wood. Young Wiglaf stayed, and when his own shield burned he sheltered behind the king's. The iron held long enough. Fire still does poorly against it.

sigurds_handshield.name: Sigurd's Handshield
sigurds_handshield.unidentified_name: a small gilt buckler painted with a coiled serpent
sigurds_handshield.lore: The saga of the Volsungs describes Sigurd riding into the hall of King Gjuki. His shield was layered with red gold and painted with a dragon, dark brown above and red below, and his helmet, saddle and surcoat bore the same mark, so that everyone who saw him knew he had killed the great worm Fafnir. A rock carving at Ramsund in Sweden tells the same story in pictures. He trusted his sword Gram more than any shield, and so he carried a small one.

carolingian_kite.name: Carolingian Kite
carolingian_kite.unidentified_name: an almond-shaped shield with a long lower point
carolingian_kite.lore: Dealers call this pattern Carolingian, though the riders of Charlemagne carried round shields. The long kite came two centuries later, and the Bayeux Tapestry shows it on nearly every Norman arm at Hastings. A horseman's left leg hangs exposed below a round shield. Somebody stretched the bottom edge into a point to cover it from knee to ankle, and within a lifetime every knight from Sicily to Scotland rode behind one. A lance point skids off the long curve.

heater_of_the_black_prince.name: Heater of the Black Prince
heater_of_the_black_prince.unidentified_name: a flat-topped black shield bearing three white feathers
heater_of_the_black_prince.lore: Edward of Woodstock commanded a wing at Crecy when he was sixteen. His father refused to send help and said to let the boy win his spurs. Ten years later at Poitiers he captured the king of France. His badge for tournaments was a black shield with three white ostrich feathers and the motto Ich dien, I serve, which the Princes of Wales still use. He died a year before his father and never reigned. His shield, helm and gauntlets are still kept at his tomb in Canterbury.

mameluke_targe.name: Mameluke Targe
mameluke_targe.unidentified_name: a small round shield inlaid with golden arabesques
mameluke_targe.lore: The Mamluks were bought as boys on the steppe, raised in barracks in Cairo, and trained for years with bow, lance and saber. In 1250 they took Egypt from their masters. Ten years later at Ain Jalut, under Qutuz and Baybars, they gave a Mongol army its first great defeat. Napoleon broke their charge at the Pyramids in 1798 and admired them so much that he took a Mamluk squadron into his own guard. The little steel shield is made for saber work on horseback.

o_tate_of_the_samurai.name: O-Tate of the Samurai
o_tate_of_the_samurai.unidentified_name: a tall lacquered wooden screen on a single leg
o_tate_of_the_samurai.lore: A samurai needed both hands for the bow and later for the sword, so Japan never took to the shield a man carries. It used the tate instead: a plank screen as tall as a man, with a hinged prop behind, set up in rows to make a wall that archers and gunners could work from. At Nagashino in 1575 Oda Nobunaga put his gunners behind stockades and screens, and the charging horsemen of the Takeda clan never reached them. Arrows and shot thud into it and stay there.

skidbladnir_aegis.name: Skidbladnir Aegis
skidbladnir_aegis.unidentified_name: a pale shield carved with miniature ship-figures
skidbladnir_aegis.lore: The dwarf sons of Ivaldi built the ship Skidbladnir for the god Freyr. It was large enough to carry all the gods with their weapons, it had a fair wind the moment its sail went up, and when the voyage was over Freyr could fold it like a cloth and put it in his pouch. Some lesser smith carved its likeness on this pale shield and caught a little of the trick. Cold folds itself away before it reaches the bearer.

smoking_mirror_of_tezcatlipoca.name: Smoking Mirror of Tezcatlipoca
smoking_mirror_of_tezcatlipoca.unidentified_name: a round shield faced with polished black obsidian
smoking_mirror_of_tezcatlipoca.lore: Tezcatlipoca, the Aztec god of night and sorcery, carried an obsidian mirror that showed not the future but the souls of those who looked into it. Quetzalcoatl saw his own ugly face in it and fled in shame, beginning the long unraveling that ended in conquest. When an enemy throws a spell at this shield, the shield turns the spell around and shows the caster what he meant to do. Most casters do not enjoy the lesson.

vajra_paramita.name: Vajra Paramita
vajra_paramita.unidentified_name: a small round shield inscribed with a thunderbolt
vajra_paramita.lore: The vajra is both thunderbolt and diamond: the thing that cannot be broken and breaks everything else. Hindu tradition says the sage Dadhichi gave up his life so the gods could make it from his bones, and Indra killed the drought-serpent Vritra with it. Buddhists took the vajra for the mind that nothing shatters. Their six perfections are giving, discipline, patience, effort, meditation and wisdom, and they carry a soul to the far shore. This shield is marked with both ideas.

horse_armor_of_the_norns.name: Horse-Armor of the Norns
horse_armor_of_the_norns.unidentified_name: a kite shield carved with three women at a well
horse_armor_of_the_norns.lore: Three women sit by the well under the World Tree. Their names are Urd, Verdandi and Skuld: what was, what is becoming, and what is owed. Each day they water the tree's roots with white clay from the well so that it will not rot, and they cut the fate of every newborn child. The gods hold their court beside them and cannot overrule them. The three figures carved on this shield return what is sent against it. A spell is a debt like any other.

scarab_of_apophis_binding.name: Scarab of Apophis-Binding
scarab_of_apophis_binding.unidentified_name: a round shield carved as a green stone beetle
scarab_of_apophis_binding.lore: Every night the sun god Ra sails his boat through the underworld, and every night the serpent Apophis rises to swallow it. Set stands in the prow and spears him. The priests at Karnak helped from above: they made a serpent of wax, wrote the name on it, spat on it, trampled it and burned it, reading from the Book of Overthrowing Apophis. At dawn Khepri the scarab rolls the sun up over the horizon. This green stone beetle is cut with those spells, and it turns malice back.

yamas_dharma_watch.name: Yama's Dharma-Watch
yamas_dharma_watch.unidentified_name: a black iron kite shield with a buffalo-horn crest
yamas_dharma_watch.lore: The oldest hymns of India say Yama was the first mortal to die. He found the road to the other world, and so became its king. He rides a black buffalo and carries a noose for drawing out the soul. In Tibet he wears the buffalo's head himself and holds up the mirror of karma, in which the dead see every act of their lives. This shield was forged from the mirror's rim. Whatever is aimed at its bearer is weighed first, and much of it is found wanting.
